Auto-summary (auto-generated may be imperfect):
OrbitFlow is evaluating Redwood Inference as a partner for hybrid GPU hosting and private VPC onramp. Key concerns: VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 audit trail, throughput targets for batch inference, and cost comparisons between dedicated vs hosted. Redwood AE+SE outlined partner onboarding steps, PoC scope, and initial benchmarks. Next steps: share partner deck and pricing spreadsheet, provide benchmark scripts and network diagrams, schedule PoC kickoff.

Topics detected: partner onboarding, VPC/peering, KMS/HSM, SOC2 / compliance, benchmarking plan, PoC scope and timelines, pricing and contract model, integration points for OrbitFlow's SaaS gateway.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Sofia's our SE, Liam's on as observer. Who do we have from OrbitFlow?
[00:06] Marcus Liu: Marcus here, head of platform. Hi all.
[00:08] Anya Petrova: Anya, cloud architect. Sorry, small delay, had to grab the network diagram.
[00:12] Diego Ramos: Diego, CTO. Happy to be here.
[00:15] Jordan Blake: Awesome. Quick agenda: partner introduction, high-level infra and security constraints, PoC goals and metrics, and then open Q&A. Does that work?
[00:22] Marcus Liu: Sounds good. We are looking to integrate a partner for GPU-backed inference, mix of hosted for non-sensitive workloads and private VPC for PII-adjacent pipelines.
[00:30] Sofia Patel: Great. Can you share a bit about current stack — where models live today, what's your traffic shape, p95 requirements, and who owns security/compliance?
[00:39] Anya Petrova: Right now models are primarily in our Kubernetes cluster on EKS, a couple of GPU pools running Triton for some models. Latency targets: p50 ~80ms, p95 under 350ms for chat-like workloads; batch jobs are mostly nightly. We expect spikes during feature launches — typical concurrency 200–400 requests, but some daily peaks up to 900. Security is Priya's team — she joined just now.
[01:02] Priya Nair: Hey, yep. For us the compliance checklist is SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML, enterprise KMS (Cloud KMS + HSM for keywrap). We also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and data residency in EU for certain tenants.
[01:18] Jordan Blake: Understood. Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. For Private we do a customer-controlled control plane and can integrate KMS/HSM and audit log forwarding. For the VPC connectivity — we do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your network posture.
[01:35] Diego Ramos: Can you explain the difference between Dedicated and Private in practice? We got a few answers from the RFP but want to confirm.
[01:42] Sofia Patel: Sure. Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in our managed environment — you get predictable throughput and isolation, but control plane is hosted by Redwood. Private means we bundle a private control plane that can be placed in your VPC or on-prem, networked to your environment, and you keep the plane. For strict compliance/regulatory needs Private is the right choice. Dedicated is lower ops for you but less control over the control plane.
[02:03] Marcus Liu: Ok — from a cost perspective, any ballpark numbers to compare reserved Dedicated vs Private on our infra?
[02:10] Jordan Blake: We have pricing ranges but we'll send a tailored spreadsheet. Ballpark — Dedicated reserved monthlies for standard A100-class pools vs Private (bring your infra) which has a platform fee plus engineering onboarding. We'll send numbers; Sofia will include sample TCO calc.
[02:23] Anya Petrova: Important: we run quantized models (int8) and some custom kernels; will Redwood runtime preserve those optimizations?
[02:31] Sofia Patel: Good question. Our runtime supports quantized models and common custom op patterns. For very custom kernels we can compile or provide a compatibility shim. We also do kernel selection based on sequence length and will surface any degradation in quantized paths. We'll need to test your model binaries in our bench script.
[02:52] Diego Ramos: Benchmarks — what's the typical PoC look like? We want to validate latency p50/p95, throughput, and memory/KV cache behavior with our workload.
[03:01] Jordan Blake: Typical PoC: 2–4 week window. We do an initial smoke test with sample traffic, then a focused benchmark run where we run your real prompts at target concurrency. Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, GPU utilization, and recommendation on batching/quantization settings. We'll also include automated regression tests against your prompts.
[03:18] Marcus Liu: Timeline-wise, we want to start a PoC in ~3 weeks if legal and security sign off. Any blockers you foresee?
[03:25] Sofia Patel: Depends on network setup and NDA. If you can provide a test model and sample traffic and grant us temporary access to an isolated VPC peering we can start benching quickly. Security docs and SOC2 artifacts usually take a couple days to share.
[03:40] Anya Petrova: About keys — we want to use our KMS for key wrapping; can Redwood support HSM-backed keywrap so data in transit and at rest meets our policy?
[03:48] Sofia Patel: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with a Redwood-managed KMS but can offer a bring-your-own-key option for Dedicated with some extra controls. For full HSM integration you should expect an onboarding step where keys are validated and rotation policies applied.
[04:08] Priya Nair: Also need to verify retention policies — logs, request payloads, and model artifacts. We can't allow raw customer PII to be stored by a third party in some cases.
[04:16] Jordan Blake: We have retention controls per-route and tokenization options. For Private we can guarantee no customer request payloads are persisted outside your environment. We'll add that to the security checklist.
[04:28] Diego Ramos: Network: do you support PrivateLink? Our infra team prefers it over VPC peering for cross-account connectivity.
[04:34] Sofia Patel: Yes, PrivateLink and VPC peering are supported; choice depends on cross-account routing and whether you want managed endpoints. We'll ask for your VPC CIDR and a diagram — that's in the action items.
[04:47] Marcus Liu: Great. On the SLA side, what's realistic? We need predictable p95 and some uptime guarantees for production.
[04:54] Jordan Blake: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs at certain tiers. For Private, SLAs are part of the enterprise contract and depend on how much we manage vs you. We'll surface typical SLOs in the partner pack.
[05:10] Anya Petrova: One more technical: do you have tracing hooks / open telemetry so we can correlate inference latency inside our APM?
[05:16] Sofia Patel: Yes, we provide tracing hooks and per-request metadata that can be forwarded to your APM. We also provide per-token cost breakdowns which is handy for chargeback.
[05:27] Jordan Blake: Quick note — a couple of our partners (integration patterns doc) and the partner deck are here: https://redwood.ai/partners/partner-deck and I'll send the private link to benchmarks.
[05:36] Marcus Liu: Please do.
[05:38] [06:00] Short pause for screen share; Anya shares a network diagram via chat.
[06:14] Anya Petrova: The diagram shows EKS clusters in eu-west-1, two private subnets for GPU workloads, public lb for API gateway, and a transit VPC. We'd prefer the private control plane to live in our transit VPC.
[06:29] Sofia Patel: That fits our Private deployment patterns. We'll just need a small set of routes and a service account. For the Peering we typically ask for a dedicated subnet to host the control plane or a peering endpoint for PrivateLink.
[06:45] Diego Ramos: On onboarding effort — what's the typical timeline and who from Redwood helps with the infra work?
[06:52] Jordan Blake: Our Professional Services (PS) team supports Private onboards; typical timeline 4–6 weeks for Private full setup, Dedicated is faster — usually 1–2 weeks to reserve capacity and connect. PS does the initial network/security validations.
[07:05] Marcus Liu: Security will want to run a scan / pentest before we go live. Are you ok with that?
[07:10] Priya Nair: We'll need to schedule a pen test window where Redwood confirms allowed scope.
[07:15] Jordan Blake: Absolutely. We sign a scoping agreement and coordinate.
[07:19] Anya Petrova: For the PoC data — do you have a way to scrub or tokenise PII in transit so we can send sample traces?
[07:26] Sofia Patel: We have tokenization tooling and data masking options in the PoC harness. We'll work with your security team to agree on what is allowed.
[07:40] [08:00] Q&A and deeper dive — Sofia goes into runtime optimizations for KV cache and batching.
[08:10] Sofia Patel: On KV cache: our runtime maintains per-session KV caches and allows pinned cache sharding for long-running chat flows to reduce recomputation. For batching, we have continuous batching that optimizes GPU utilization while keeping latency SLOs. You can configure max batch size and latency thresholds.
[08:31] Marcus Liu: Do you handle cache eviction transparently? We need predictable memory usage.
[08:36] Sofia Patel: Yes, eviction policies are configurable, and we'll benchmark memory footprint with your session lengths. For persistent sessions we recommend cache pinning on Dedicated/Private.
[08:48] Diego Ramos: Any constraints around custom operators or compiled libs? We do have a couple of proprietary C++ kernels.
[08:55] Sofia Patel: We can ingest custom wheels or container images and run compatibility checks. For Private deployments we can run them in your environment to reduce EULA surface. We'll need to check ABI compatibility.
[09:08] Marcus Liu: About billing — can we get per-route metering so product teams can be charged back?
[09:14] Jordan Blake: Yes, per-route and token-level metering is available in the Console; we can export to your billing system or provide daily usage CSVs.
[09:23] Anya Petrova: For model updates in production, can we pin versions and do canary rollouts?
[09:29] Sofia Patel: Yes, the platform supports pinned versions, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variants if regressions are detected. We'll demo that in the next session.
[09:40] [10:15] Marcus Liu: Competitor question — you've heard of ApexCloud and TitanServe — any differentiators we should be aware of?
[10:23] Jordan Blake: On the main differentiators: Redwood emphasizes production economics — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, deep batching/kv/cache optimizations, and an ops-first Console. From a partner integration standpoint we prioritize predictable latency and routing controls.
[10:40] Diego Ramos: Ok, let's get to PoC specifics. We propose a 2-week bench: week 1 smoke + model compatibility; week 2 performance at target concurrency (900 peak). Deliverables: p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, cost estimates per 1M tokens. Are you ok with that?
[10:59] Sofia Patel: Yes. We'll need a test model — either your exported model or we can use a close open checkpoint. Also, provide sample prompt set and a traffic replay tool or dataset.
[11:10] Marcus Liu: We can provide a replay of 48 hours of anonymized call traffic, plus a smaller spike file for the concurrency tests.
[11:18] Jordan Blake: Perfect. We'll also include a quick evaluation harness that runs the tests and collects traces.
[11:26] [11:40] Discussion about access and credentials — vault integration and temporary service accounts.
[11:44] Priya Nair: For temporary accounts we require short-lived credentials and we want to review the keys usage logs.
[11:50] Sofia Patel: We'll use IAM roles and short-lived tokens; logs will be sent to your SIEM.
[12:00] Marcus Liu: Great. Any blockers from Redwood's side in terms of compliance?
[12:05] Jordan Blake: We'll send our SOC2 report and pen test artifacts. For Private we'll do a joint review.
[12:12] Anya Petrova: Network detail — we'll need the IP ranges and the contact for the network engineer.
[12:17] Jordan Blake: Noted. We'll include a template network diagram and a checklist in the partner pack.
[12:25] Diego Ramos: If we move to Private, what's the expected on-call model — who owns incident response at night?
[12:32] Sofia Patel: For fully managed Private with PS support, Redwood offers a 24/7 on-call for the platform layer; responsibilities are listed in the SOW. For partially managed we'll provide playbooks and a pager rotation for escalations.
[12:47] Marcus Liu: Ok, sounds like next steps are clear.
[12:52] Jordan Blake: Recap — we'll share the partner deck, security pack, and a tailored pricing spreadsheet. Sofia will share the bench harness and initial test config. OrbitFlow to share network diagram, anonymized traffic replay, and the list of models. We'll aim to kickoff PoC in three weeks.
[13:13] Anya Petrova: Confirming, and we'll add Priya as security contact to the ticket.
[13:18] Jordan Blake: Perfect. Any final questions?
[13:22] Diego Ramos: Not from me. Thanks.
[13:24] Jordan Blake: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links.

[13:40] End of recording (automated timestamp summary may be approximate).

Redwood to share partner deck, security pack, benchmark harness and pricing. OrbitFlow to share network diagram, anonymized traffic replay, and model artifacts.
